subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Type 1 diabetes is caused by:
options: The kidneys failing to filter glucose
The body's cells not responding to insulin
The pancreas not producing enough (or any) insulin
questions.explain: In Type 1 diabetes the pancreas produces little or no insulin, so it is usually treated with insulin injections.

questions.q: What is homeostasis?
options: The breakdown of glucose for energy
The maintenance of a constant internal environment
questions.explain: Homeostasis is the regulation of internal conditions, such as temperature and blood glucose, within set limits.

questions.q: Negative feedback in homeostasis works by:
options: Reinforcing a change so it grows larger
Detecting a change and triggering a response that reverses it back to normal
questions.explain: Negative feedback reverses changes: if a level rises too high, a response lowers it back towards the normal value.

questions.q: Compared with nervous responses, hormonal responses are generally:
questions.explain: Hormonal responses are slower to act but their effects last longer than fast, short-lived nervous responses.

questions.q: Urea, which is removed by the kidneys, is produced in the liver from the breakdown of excess:
questions.explain: The liver breaks down excess amino acids in a process called deamination, forming urea that the kidneys excrete.

questions.q: How do plant roots respond to gravity?
options: They do not respond to gravity
questions.explain: Roots show positive gravitropism, growing downwards in the direction of gravity, controlled by auxin distribution.

questions.q: Which sequence correctly traces a nervous impulse in a simple reflex?
options: Sensory neurone -> relay neurone -> motor neurone
Motor neurone -> sensory neurone -> relay neurone
Motor neurone -> relay neurone -> sensory neurone
Relay neurone -> sensory neurone -> motor neurone
questions.explain: In a reflex arc the impulse passes from the sensory neurone, through a relay neurone, to the motor neurone.

questions.q: FSH (follicle stimulating hormone) acts to:
options: Cause an egg (in a follicle) to mature in the ovary
questions.explain: FSH, secreted by the pituitary gland, stimulates eggs to mature in the ovaries and triggers oestrogen release.

questions.q: What is the correct order of structures in a reflex arc?
options: Stimulus → effector → motor → relay → sensory → receptor
Stimulus → receptor → sensory → relay → motor → effector → response
questions.explain: The reflex arc runs stimulus, receptor, sensory neurone, relay neurone, motor neurone, effector, response.

questions.q: Why are there gaps (synapses) between neurones rather than them being directly joined?
options: So impulses can travel more slowly always
So chemicals can transmit the signal, allowing connections and control between neurones
So blood can flow between them
questions.explain: Synapses use neurotransmitters to pass signals, allowing flexible connections between many neurones.

questions.q: In a knee-jerk reflex, the effector that produces the response is a:
questions.explain: The effector is the muscle that contracts to produce the response, e.g. the leg muscle making the lower leg kick.

questions.q: Hormones are transported around the body in the:
questions.explain: Hormones are chemical messengers secreted by glands and carried in the blood to target organs.

questions.q: After a sugary meal, blood glucose rises. The correct homeostatic response is for the pancreas to release:
options: Insulin, so cells take up glucose and the liver stores it as glycogen
Adrenaline, so the heart beats faster
Glucagon, so the liver releases more glucose
ADH, so more water is reabsorbed
questions.explain: High blood glucose triggers insulin release, causing cells to absorb glucose and the liver to store it as glycogen.

questions.q: Which organ monitors and controls blood glucose concentration by releasing insulin and glucagon?
questions.explain: The pancreas detects blood glucose levels and secretes insulin or glucagon to keep them within normal limits.

questions.q: Which hormone causes the lining of the uterus to thicken during the menstrual cycle?
questions.explain: Oestrogen, produced by the ovaries, causes the uterus lining to build up ready for a possible pregnancy.

questions.q: In the menstrual cycle, which hormone maintains the uterus lining in the second half of the cycle?
questions.explain: Progesterone maintains the thickened uterus lining; when its level falls, the lining breaks down and menstruation occurs.

questions.q: Light entering the eye is first refracted (bent) by the:
questions.explain: The transparent cornea does most of the refraction of light as it enters the eye.

questions.q: When you touch a hot object and pull your hand away before feeling pain, this shows that a reflex:
options: Happens before the brain consciously processes the pain
Is slower than a conscious response
questions.explain: The reflex (handled by the spinal cord) acts before the impulse reaches the conscious brain, so you react before feeling pain.

questions.q: Type 2 diabetes is associated with:
options: A complete lack of a pancreas
Too much insulin being produced from birth
The body's cells no longer responding properly to insulin
questions.explain: In Type 2 diabetes cells stop responding to insulin; it is linked to obesity and often controlled by diet and exercise.

questions.q: At a synapse, how is the signal passed from one neurone to the next?
options: The neurones touch and pass electricity directly
The impulse jumps as a spark
questions.explain: At a synapse, neurotransmitters diffuse across the gap and trigger an impulse in the next neurone.

questions.q: How does auxin cause a shoot to bend towards light?
options: Auxin destroys cells on the shaded side
Auxin stops all growth on the lit side
Auxin builds up on the lit side, making it grow faster
Auxin builds up on the shaded side, making those cells elongate more
questions.explain: Auxin accumulates on the shaded side and increases cell elongation there, bending the shoot towards the light.

questions.q: When blood glucose falls too low, the pancreas releases glucagon, which causes the liver to:
questions.explain: Glucagon makes the liver convert stored glycogen back into glucose, raising blood glucose levels.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel GCSE (9–1) Biology (1BI0) specification; Animal Coordination Homeostasis
